PR 1 of TRD: TRD: Configurable Tasks Backend - Kata Adapter. Contains 16 tasks. Shippable state: After this PR, a project that sets `tracker: kata` in its toolchain configuration has both the tracker and work-graph categories resolve to kata, `toolchain-cli preflight` reports the kata version, and an absent, too-old, or unbound kata stops preflight with a named message before any work item is written; projects without kata configuration see no change.

## Task: TRD-001
## References
TRD: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-6995dc96-configurable-tasks-backend-kata.md
TRD Task: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-6995dc96-configurable-tasks-backend-kata.md#trd-001
PRD: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-6995dc96-configurable-tasks-backend-kata.md
PRD Requirement: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-6995dc96-configurable-tasks-backend-kata.md#req-016
PRD Requirement: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-6995dc96-configurable-tasks-backend-kata.md#req-012
PRD ACs: AC-012-1, AC-016-1, AC-016-3
Parent Epic: [trd:trd-2026-6995dc96-configurable-tasks-backend-kata]
Read-first: read the TRD, TRD Task section, PRD and PRD Requirement above before any work on this bead.


--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-016**: The skip guarantee must cover every kata-dependent check, not only the suite that ships with the adapter. [Must]
The skip guarantee must cover every kata-dependent check, not only the suite that ships with the adapter. [Must] REQ-012 guarantees that installation and the adapter's own suite tolerate the tool's absence. This extends that guarantee to checks added elsewhere in the repo as the effort grows, and to proving that the skips are honest rather than silently vacuous.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-012-1: Given a machine with the kata tool absent | When the package is installed and its test suite is run | Then installation succeeds and the suite reports skips naming the missing tool rather than failures
- AC-016-1: Given a runner with the backing tool absent | When the repo-wide test run is executed | Then it exits successfully and names each skipped check with the reason "tool absent"
- AC-016-3: Given the skip list | When it is compared to the set of tests that touch kata | Then no test that asserts kata behavior is reported as passing on a runner where the tool is absent

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-012**: Kata must be an optional dependency, never an installation requirement. [Must] [RISK: kata is an external binary this repo does not version; adapter health, detection and tests must all tolerate its absence]
Kata must be an optional dependency, never an installation requirement. [Must] [RISK: kata is an external binary this repo does not version; adapter health, detection and tests must all tolerate its absence] Installing Ensemble must not start requiring the kata tool, and every check that assumes it must be able to report absence without failing installation, generation, or the rest of the suite.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-012-1: Given a machine with the kata tool absent | When the package is installed and its test suite is run | Then installation succeeds and the suite reports skips naming the missing tool rather than failures
- AC-016-1: Given a runner with the backing tool absent | When the repo-wide test run is executed | Then it exits successfully and names each skipped check with the reason "tool absent"
- AC-016-3: Given the skip list | When it is compared to the set of tests that touch kata | Then no test that asserts kata behavior is reported as passing on a runner where the tool is absent

--- TRD Context ---
**Verified baseline.** Read from the repository and the installed kata binary (v0.23.0 at `/opt/homebrew/bin/kata`).

- `tracker.yaml` v1.1 declares 18 capabilities: 4 required (`tracker.show`, `tracker.create`, `tracker.update`, `tracker.close`) and 14 optional, the newest being `tracker.label-one` (`addedInMinor: 1`) (`docs/toolchain/contracts/tracker.md:7`). `work-graph.yaml` v2.0 declares 3 optional capabilities, naming `work-graph-links-fallback` (`packages/development/toolchain/categories/work-graph.yaml:5-27`).
- Coverage differs by adapter. Beads declares all 17 tracker capabilities and all 3 work-graph capabilities (`packages/development/skills/adapter-tracker-beads/adapter.yaml`, `contract: {tracker: "1.0", work-graph: "2.0"}`). Jira (`packages/infrastructure/skills/adapter-tracker-jira/adapter.yaml`) and azure-boards (`packages/infrastructure/skills/adapter-tracker-azure-boards/adapter.yaml`) each declare `categories: [tracker]`, 8 tracker capabilities, and no work-graph capability.
- The graph fallback is partial. `work-graph-links-fallback` serves `ready` and `plan` only. `graph-health` returns `NOT_ALLOWED` (`packages/development/lib/toolchain/builtin/work-graph-links-fallback.js:279-287`), although the contract names this fallback for graph-health. `plan` appends unorderable items instead of reporting them (`:256`). The fallback orders topologically only when `tracker.show` supplies `dependencies` (`:311-322`). No shipped tracker maps that field, so the fallback is not dependency-aware on any shipped backend (reviewer-confirmed).
- Routing tests only the category claim: `trackerProvidesWorkGraph` checks `manifest.categories` (`packages/development/lib/toolchain/work-graph-resolve.js:77-79`). On that path `source` is the work-graph category default, not the tracker's (`:84`), which breaks AC-001-1.
- `tracker.list` with no `parse` block returns raw stdout (`packages/development/lib/toolchain/runner.js:1170-1171`). Beads, jira, and azure-boards leave it unmapped for that reason. A mapped list would be validated against `work-item.json`, which requires a top-level `id` (`runner.js:618-620`), so it fails unless `CAPABILITY_NORMALIZED_SCHEMA` routes it to a collection schema (`runner.js:601-604`).
  - Kata facts come from `kata <command> --help`, `kata quickstart`, and read-only `kata doctor --json` and `kata list --json` run in an unbound scratch directory, plus a live write-side capture in a scratch project bound with `kata init --project trd-capture-scratch` against kata v0.23.0 under an isolated `KATA_HOME` (2026-11-14; raw envelopes `~/.omp/trd-6995dc96/capture/*.json`, summary `~/.omp/trd-6995dc96/kata-envelope-facts.md`). Confirmed there: every envelope carries `kata_api_version`; the ref identifier is `short_id`; `--meta ensemble_external_key=<key>` round-trips as `issue.metadata.ensemble_external_key`; `list --meta k=v` filters exactly; `show.links[]` carries `{from, to, type}` edges; `list` returns `{complete, truncated, issues[]}` with no total; `close --evidence <type>:<value>` is accepted; `set-status` and a bulk or multi-id form do not exist. Kata still has no plan, graph-health, or export command and no type field. It has `ready` (open items not blocked by open items), blocking edges (`edit --blocked-by`), typed close evidence, and ownership (`claim`).

### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Manifest-only tracker adapter | `adapter-tracker-kata` declares `tracker` only. Work-graph stays on the built-in fallback. No engine change. | Smallest diff. Same shape as shipped jira and azure-boards. No new code path. REQ-013 trivially preserved. | Fails AC-001-1 and AC-006-2: the work-graph adapter resolved is the built-in, which reports its own identity and a default `source`. Fails AC-007-4: the envelope names the built-in, not kata. Fails AC-007-3 and AC-007-5: no graph-health source exists, because the built-in returns `NOT_ALLOWED`. Meets AC-007-2 only if kata's `tracker.show` maps `dependencies` [UNVERIFIED]. The PRD's own ACs still require the tracker amendments (AC-003-3 test evidence, AC-004-2 owner), so "no engine change" does not hold. |
| B. Graph operations on the tracker contract | Add additive tracker 1.1 capabilities `tracker.ready`, `tracker.plan`, `tracker.graph-health`. Leave work-graph untouched. | One category answers every tracker question. Independent of work-graph auto-routing. | Duplicates `work-graph.*`, so ready, plan, and graph-health each have two answers. Every graph consumer moves: `packages/development/skills/ensemble-beads-build-wave/SKILL.md:26` requires `work-graph.ready`, and PRD REQ-011 exists to prevent that churn. Kata still needs C's analyzer, so B pays C's engine cost plus a second surface. Contradicts REQ-001, which requires kata to declare the `work-graph` category. |
| C. Attach through `work-graph` v2.0 with one shared analyzer | Kata declares `tracker` and `work-graph`. `work-graph.ready` is native (`kata ready --json`). `work-graph.plan` and `work-graph.graph-health` declare `provider: work-graph-analyzer`, served by the existing built-in analyzer, extended with graph-health and findings. Contracts amended additively: tracker 1.0 to 1.1, work-graph 2.0 to 2.1. | Matches the PRD's declared categories. `tracker: kata` alone selects kata for both categories (AC-001-1, AC-006-2). Reuses the shipped ready and ordering code, adding no subsystem. Makes the graph-health fallback reference true. Beads (`bv`) and jira keep their current paths. | Three engine edits: resolver capability test and source fix, provider dispatch, and analyzer identity, graph-health, and findings. Plan and health cost one `tracker.show` per item unless `kata list --json` carries edges [UNVERIFIED]. The analyzer is shared, not kata-native, so the PRD must say so (Open Question 9). It changes jira's graph-health answer (Open Question 13). |

**Pick: C.**

**Rationale:**

- **Against A.** A is cheap because it stops short of the requirement. If A declares `work-graph`, plan and health have no provider and graph-health has no source. If A leaves work-graph undeclared, the resolved work-graph adapter is the built-in, so AC-001-1, AC-006-2, and AC-007-4 fail. The gap is computation and identity, not configuration. No YAML can emit a cycle finding, a `dependencyAware: true` for a backend with no plan command, or kata as the serving adapter. A also pays the tracker amendments (owner, close evidence), so the only work it avoids is the analyzer work that C needs too.
- **Against B.** B moves the same computation to another category and creates a parallel answer. Every consumer that requires `work-graph.ready` changes, and the analyzer is still required, so B costs C's engine work plus a second surface. It also contradicts the PRD's declared category set.
- **Why C adds the least machinery.** Each change extends a seam the code already has: a capability entry in `packages/development/toolchain/schemas/adapter-manifest-schema.json`, the in-process work-graph branch in `packages/development/lib/toolchain-cli.js:470-482` and `:539-547`, the analyzer that already computes ready and plan (`builtin/work-graph-links-fallback.js:211-258`), and the category contracts. No new subsystem duplicates `packages/development/lib/toolchain/`. Adapter directories hold data: `validateAdapterDir` (`packages/development/lib/toolchain/validate.js:762-788`) checks the manifest, allowlist, conformance, and credentials, and the runner executes only manifest argv templates (`runner.js:1261`). The one in-process capability path is the built-in module that `work-graph-resolve.js` already loads. A JavaScript module inside the adapter directory was therefore rejected.
- **The strengthened fallback.** Every work-graph answer states `dependencyAware`, and the serving adapter is named in the envelope. `plan` reports unorderable items as `findings` instead of appending them. Routing requires all three work-graph capabilities. No shipped tracker changes routing: beads declares all three, and jira and azure-boards do not claim the category.
- **Costs accepted.** C is the only option that meets the work-graph ACs, and the only one that changes engine code. Plan and health fan out one `tracker.show` per item. Each per-item call must share the capability's class bound, or N individually bounded calls are unbounded in total. The first implementation step measures this before the kata tests are accepted.
Satisfies: REQ-016, REQ-012
Target File: packages/development/tests/helpers/kata-guard.js, packages/development/tests/helpers/kata-scratch.js, packages/development/tests/fixtures/kata/
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given the kata binary is absent from PATH, when a kata-dependent test runs through the guard, then the test is reported skipped with reason "tool absent" and the run does not fail.
- [ ] Given the kata binary is present, when the harness creates a scratch workspace, then it binds that workspace under an isolated KATA_HOME and never reads or writes a real project.
- [ ] Given a scratch workspace with seeded items, when the harness runs list, show, ready and status, then their JSON envelopes are recorded as fixtures that every later mapping task reads.
- [ ] Given a test finishes, when the harness tears down, then the scratch workspace and its daemon state are removed.
Dependencies:

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-018**: Selecting the new backend in a workspace it cannot serve must be caught before any work item is written. [Must]
Selecting the new backend in a workspace it cannot serve must be caught before any work item is written. [Must] Misconfiguration that REQ-001 and REQ-012 do not already cover — a workspace that is not bound, a tool version too old for a required operation — is caught during preflight, before the flow creates, edits, or closes anything. Goals and Non-Goals Goals A project selects its tasks backend by editing one configuration value, and the TRD-to-work-items flow works end to end on that backend with no beads tool installed. *(REQ-001, REQ-009, REQ-014)* Dependency-aware pickup, sequential planning, and graph-health triage work on the new backend, not only on the backend that shipped with the machinery. *(REQ-007)* No command, skill or agent name states which tasks backend it uses. *(REQ-009, REQ-011)* A project that never hears about the new backend sees zero behavior change. *(REQ-013)* The capability coverage of both backends is stated where a reader would look for it, and provably complete against the contract. *(REQ-015)* Non-Goals Making the new backend the default, or migrating anyone onto it. Selection stays explicit; unconfigured projects keep today's tracker. *(REQ-013)* A migration tool from Beads to Kata. Importing an existing `.beads/issues.jsonl` into a kata project, and the reverse, are out of scope; teams start a fresh backlog or keep beads. Third or fourth backends. Exactly two backends ship. The `jira` adapter stays as authored: it deliberately implements the tracker contract only and lets `work-graph` take the built-in analyzer. Nothing here pulls it onto the graph path. Changing what a TRD contains, or how it is authored. `create-trd` already reaches no tracker: it writes the TRD document. Requirement coverage, task format, shippable-state and design-readiness rules are unchanged. A compatibility window or deprecation period for the retired command name. Per the retirement precedent, removal is outright. *(REQ-009)* Scheduling, dispatch, retries, or recovery in Kata. Owning the work-item record is the whole claim; running agents against it stays outside Ensemble. Backfilling historical PRD and TRD documents. Archived documents keep their original wording, including the retired command name where they used it. Relationship to Existing PRDs Ratified in this run: this PRD extends the toolchain line of work rather than superseding it. The three documents below carry amendment notes at their next edit; none is reopened. | Document | Standing | Relationship | |---|---|---| | `PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer` | Locked, 2026-10-21 | Parent. Its exit criterion is that the tracker swap "is demonstrated end-to-end, by configuration alone", and REQ-020 already overrides the sole-execution-layer claim below. Kata is the second demonstration; it is the first that exercises the `work-graph` capabilities natively, which `jira` left on the built-in fallback. | | `PRD-2026-b6939c7c-config-driven-tools` | Draft, 2026-08-13 | Partially superseded, before this PRD. REQ-015 ("Beads remains the sole execution layer") and the non-goal "Migrating Beads off execution layer" were already overridden by 8d825f54 REQ-020. This PRD inherits that override and adds nothing new against it. Its Layer 1 and Layer 3 work — project-local configuration, provider-neutral prose, CI enforcement — is the foundation this PRD builds on, and its CI enforcement (no hardcoded backend references in prompts and skills) is treated as a check to satisfy, not a rule to re-litigate. | | `PRD-2026-023-multi-trd-beads-workstream` | 2026-06-16 | Non-goal conflict, resolved by scoping. Its non-goal "replacing Beads with another task graph system" is not contradicted: beads is not replaced, and stays default. Its multi-TRD workstream behavior is stated in beads terms; whatever of it must survive on kata is carried here as REQ-007 and REQ-008 rather than reopened there. | | `PRD-2026-87e64cc6-command-surface-consolidation` | 2026-10-06 | Precedent, followed. Its 2026-10-18 amendment retired variant commands by folding them into base-command flags and deleting the aliases outright, with no compatibility window (REQ-008 there). REQ-009 here applies the same retirement to the last backend-named TRD command. | Terminology. The user-facing request says "tasks backend"; the repository's toolchain axis is named `tracker` (category `tracker`, contract `tracker.md`, `tracker.*` capabilities), with `work-graph` as the dependency-graph category. This PRD keeps `tracker` as the technical name and treats "tasks backend" as the product-level phrase for a resolved tracker adapter. Approvals and Decision Ownership | Decision | Approving role | Criteria judged against | |---|---|---| | Adding a second tasks backend, and the adapter shape it takes | Architecture owner | `PRD-2026-8d825f54`'s locked contract; the constitution's approval requirement for architecture changes. Recorded as ratified in this run: extend, do not supersede. | | Removing a shipped command name outright | Command-surface owner | `PRD-2026-87e64cc6` REQ-008's no-compatibility-window precedent, ratified in this run. | | Keeping beads as the shipped default | Product owner | REQ-013; zero delta for unconfigured projects. | | Scope of native capability coverage in the new adapter | Architecture owner | REQ-001 AC-001-4 and REQ-015 AC-015-2: the required set plus every capability the contract marks with a fallback. Ratified in this run as tracker-plus-graph, not tracker-only. | | Whether the kata tool becomes a package dependency | Package owner | REQ-012; installation must not require it. | | Scoping the kata integration to locally-spawned kata daemons, leaving the remote kata gateway path undelivered and untested | Architecture owner | Decided 2026-11-14, recorded in `TRD-2026-6995dc96`. Two live gateway probe responses have no local analogue: sending no token gives `origin_forbidden`, sending a token that is not a valid browser session gives `web_session_required` — both `kind: internal` with `exit_code: 1`, both outside the 2/3/4/5/7 exit-code taxonomy this integration's error mapping assumes. The gateway also checks an `Origin` header the CLI controls, so an adapter cannot compensate by setting headers itself, which makes `KATA_AUTH_TOKEN` a hard prerequisite for remote use rather than an optional enhancement. Nothing below obliges anyone to reach or authenticate against a gateway. If gateway-backed delivery is wanted later, a requirement must be added covering remote-gateway authentication and its failure envelope: the 18 requirements here stop at "a Kata project" while the adapter manifest's `env` block already names `KATA_SERVER` and `KATA_AUTH_TOKEN`. | The accountable counterpart for the customer-facing approve/request-changes step is the same architecture owner who signs the adapter shape: no requirement here is approved by its author. Technical Constraints and Dependencies Constraints The backing tool must be at version v0.23.0 or later. This PRD sets that floor; it is a requirement, not an observation about the tool — nothing in this repository versions it, so the statement belongs here rather than in a lockfile. It is the referent for REQ-018 AC-018-2: a tool below the floor is a named preflight failure, not a degraded run. The first implementation that exercises the mapped operations against v0.23.0 confirms the floor holds; if it does not, this constraint is wrong and is corrected by reopening this PRD, not by patching the adapter to compensate. *(REQ-012, REQ-018)* The tool stays an optional dependency: no constraint here may make its absence fail installation, generation, or a test run. *(REQ-012, REQ-016)* Adapter coverage is asserted against the versioned contract documents — `docs/toolchain/contracts/tracker.md` (contract version `1.1` as amended 2026-11-14, previously `1.0`) and `docs/toolchain/contracts/work-graph.md` (contract version `2.0`) — so "the required set" in REQ-001 AC-001-4 and REQ-015 AC-015-2 has a dated referent rather than a moving one. A bump of either contract version is a requirements change to this PRD, not an implementation detail. Beads remains the shipped default; nothing here licenses selecting the new backend by inference. *(REQ-013)* Delivery is against locally-spawned kata daemons. This effort configures, exercises and tests the adapter against a kata daemon started on the same machine as the flow that calls it; operation against a remote kata gateway is not delivered and not tested here. *(REQ-001, REQ-012, REQ-018)* Declared dependencies on other documents | Document | Role here | Enforced by | |---|---|---| | `PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer` (Locked) | Parent contract; its capability definitions and exit criterion are what this PRD satisfies | REQ-001 AC-001-4, REQ-015 AC-015-2 | | `docs/toolchain/contracts/tracker.md` (contract version `1.1`, amended 2026-11-14), `work-graph.md` (contract version `2.0`) | The required-plus-fallback-bearing capability set | REQ-001 AC-001-4, REQ-015 AC-015-1 | | `PRD-2026-b6939c7c-config-driven-tools` | Foundation: project-local configuration, provider-neutral prose, CI enforcement of no hardcoded backend references | REQ-011 | | `PRD-2026-87e64cc6-command-surface-consolidation` | Retirement precedent — outright removal, no compatibility window | REQ-009 | | `PRD-2026-023-multi-trd-beads-workstream` | Behavior carried forward in beads terms, re-expressed here rather than reopened there | REQ-007, REQ-008 | | Backing tool at v0.23.0+ (external, unversioned by this repo) | The operations the adapter maps onto | REQ-001, REQ-012, REQ-018 | Entry Criteria Before implementation starts: 1. The `kata` tool is available on the implementation machine, and a scratch kata project exists that a test harness can create and discard without touching a real project. *(prerequisite for REQ-001 through REQ-008; REQ-012 makes its absence a skip, not a blocker to the rest)* 2. The capability inventory in `docs/toolchain/contracts/tracker.md` and `work-graph.md` is confirmed current, since REQ-001 AC-001-4 and REQ-015 AC-015-2 assert against it. 3. The list of commands, agents and skills naming the beads-specific command is enumerated, so REQ-009's "no entry remains" is checkable rather than impressionistic. 4. Generation and validation entry points (`generate`, `validate`, the contract-docs check) are confirmed runnable locally, since REQ-009 and REQ-015 are asserted through generated artifacts. 5. A beads project fixture exists that exercises the TRD flow end to end, so REQ-010 AC-010-2 and REQ-011 AC-011-3 can be compared against before-and-after output rather than asserted from reading. Exit Criteria Effort is delivered when all of the following are observable: 1. Setting one configuration value in a project with no beads tool installed produces a scaffolded kata backlog with dependency edges, a ready list, and a sequential plan, from the backend-neutral command. *(REQ-001, REQ-007, REQ-009, REQ-014)* 2. A capability-coverage assertion passes for the kata adapter against the full required-plus-fallback-bearing set in both contracts, and fails when a capability is removed from the manifest. *(REQ-001 AC-001-4, REQ-015 AC-015-2)* 3. No source manifest or generated artifact names the retired command; the dispatcher rejects the retired name and names the replacement. *(REQ-009)* 4. The backend-neutral command accepts every phase the retired command supported, and a beads project produces byte-identical work items before and after. *(REQ-010)* 5. A project with no toolchain configuration resolves to beads, the shipped default configuration file is unchanged, and no tracker detection route selects the new backend from repository contents — a repository carrying a Kata workspace binding file with no toolchain configuration still resolves to beads. *(REQ-013)* 6. Installing the package and running its test suite on a machine without the kata tool both succeed, with kata-dependent checks reported as named skips. *(REQ-012, REQ-016)* 7. Shared command, skill and contract prose contains no tracker binary or tracker storage path outside explicitly beads-scoped sections, and the beads-scoped flow is unchanged by the prose edit. *(REQ-011)* 8. Generated contract documentation lists both backends with the native-versus-fallback split, and the docs check fails on an unrecorded manifest change. *(REQ-015)* 9. A misconfigured kata workspace stops in preflight having created zero work items, and a backing tool that hangs, fails, or emits unparseable output produces a named adapter error rather than a silent empty result. *(REQ-017, REQ-018)* Dependency Map | Requirement | Depends on | Reason | |---|---|---| | REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005 | REQ-001 | Each is a slice of one manifest; none is reachable until the adapter resolves | | REQ-006 | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005 | Fallback suppression is only observable once the capabilities the fallbacks stand in for exist | | REQ-007 | REQ-001, REQ-005 | Graph output is meaningless unless links land on real blocking edges | | REQ-008 | REQ-001 | Read paths ride the same manifest | | REQ-009 | REQ-001 | Retiring the backend-named name only makes sense once a second backend resolves | | REQ-010 | REQ-009 | Rename-and-preserve-flags is one edit; the flag set is measured from the pre-rename command | | REQ-011 | REQ-009, REQ-010 | Prose rewrite targets the neutral surface | | REQ-012 | REQ-001 | Absence handling is a property of the adapter's health and detection | | REQ-013 | REQ-001, REQ-012 | Detection-never-auto-selects matters only because a detectable candidate now exists | | REQ-014 | REQ-009, REQ-010 | Documentation describes the surviving command | | REQ-015 | REQ-001, REQ-006, REQ-007 | Coverage documentation records native versus fallback, which earlier requirements establish | | REQ-016 | REQ-001, REQ-012 | Skip-on-absence is only meaningful once there is a kata-dependent check to skip | | REQ-017 | REQ-001 | Timeouts and error passthrough are adapter behaviors, reachable only through its invocation layer | | REQ-018 | REQ-001, REQ-014, REQ-017 | Preflight gating reuses the adapter's health detection and the documented binding prerequisite | Delivery waves Shipped in this order. Wave 1 is the critical path; nothing downstream is observable until it closes. | Wave | Scope | Requirements | Cannot start until | Wave closes when | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Adapter manifest and mapping — one package, one manifest, one mapping table | REQ-001 → REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005 → REQ-006 | Entry criteria 1-2 met | Exit criterion 2 passes: coverage assertion green, and red when a capability is removed | | 2 | Graph capabilities — same package, separate capability group | REQ-007, REQ-008 | Wave 1: links land on real blocking edges | Ready list, sequential plan and graph-health all report the kata adapter as their source | | 3 | Surface rename and prose neutralization | REQ-009 → REQ-010 → REQ-011 → REQ-014 | Wave 1 in code no dependency; ships after it because REQ-009's premise is that a second backend resolves | Exit criteria 3, 4 and 7 hold; beads project output byte-identical | | 4 | Safety and disclosure | REQ-012, REQ-013 after wave 1; REQ-015 last | Waves 1-3 for REQ-015, which records what they established | Exit criteria 5 and 8 hold | | 5 | Robustness | REQ-017, REQ-018 after wave 1; REQ-016 once a kata-dependent test exists | Wave 1 for REQ-017/018; first kata-dependent test for REQ-016 | Exit criterion 9 holds | Wave 3 is the only wave with no code dependency on wave 1, so it can be built in parallel and held for ship order. REQ-015 is deliberately last in wave 4: coverage documentation records the native-versus-fallback split that waves 1-3 establish, so writing it earlier would document a set that is still moving. REQ-016 is the only wave-5 item gated on an artifact rather than a wave, because a skip guarantee has nothing to skip until a kata-dependent check exists. Readiness Scorecard | Dimension | Score | Note | |---|---|---| | Completeness | 4.8 | 18 requirements across five feature areas, including an explicit non-functional set; every Must has a happy-path and an edge-case AC; a stated external version floor and declared document dependencies now sit alongside the entry criteria | | Testability | 4.8 | ACs are observable reads of resolved configuration, item state, or generated artifacts; the ready-list ordering and the timeout bound are now checkable properties rather than adjectives, and the Should-tier AC bar is an explicit recorded rule rather than an implied one | | Clarity | 4.7 | Terminology reconciled explicitly; delivery sequence states what can be built in parallel and what each wave must show; the requirement/tool boundary is respected — the PRD states the shape of a bound and leaves values to sizing | | Feasibility | 4.6 | Contract machinery exists and a second adapter already ships against it; graph-health has a named implementation (adapter-side scan); the external tool's version floor is now pinned, so the preflight gate has a referent | | Overall | 4.7 | Above 4.0 Development Ready threshold | Notes Constitution compliance: passed. Article 3 (tests accompany features) is met by per-requirement ACs plus an Exit-criterion assertion-coverage check that can fail; Articles 4 and 8 by keeping selection in configuration and adapter manifests rather than in code; Article 6 by AC-009-1, AC-014-2 and Exit criterion 1, which run the flow through the shipped command rather than around it; Article 7 by AC-001-4 and Exit criterion 2, which require a guard shown capable of failing. AC-015-3 was also cited for Article 7 through v1.1.0; it is now stated as reader-observable drift discovery rather than as a check that demonstrably fails, so Article 7 no longer rests on it. The mechanism that makes a stale coverage record discoverable is a TRD-level choice, and the TRD SHOULD satisfy it with a guard that can be shown failing rather than a documentation note. Ambiguity scan: 0 markers. Both former `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers were resolved in the 2026-11-13 refinement pass: in-progress is represented by Kata item ownership (REQ-004), and graph-health is computed by the adapter as a local cycle and dangling-edge scan over the exported item links (REQ-007), since no backing-tool command provides it and the contract's links-only fallback implements ready-listing and planning only. Acceptance-criteria bar, stated explicitly: Must requirements carry 2+ ACs including an edge case; Should requirements carry 1+ AC, and the tier is not held to the edge-case rule. This is a recorded decision, not an omission — the Should-tier requirements (REQ-008, REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-017) were reviewed against the Must-tier bar in the 2026-11-13 v1.2.0 pass and left at their existing coverage deliberately. Decisions genuinely the user's — relationship to existing PRDs, the fate and shape of the beads-named command, whether beads stays selectable, how deep the adapter's capability coverage goes, and the two marker resolutions above — were taken in an explicit decision pass and recorded in *Relationship to Existing PRDs* and *Approvals and Decision Ownership*. Lock history: Locked on 2026-11-13 at v1.1.0, confirmed by the human at that refinement's close-out, on the record that readiness sat at 4.6 with zero open questions at that pass. Reopened to Draft the same day at v1.2.0: that pass added a delivery sequence, a version floor, and a constraints section, and rewrote three ACs — a requirements change by the lock's own definition. Nothing was invalidated by the reopen: `TRD-2026-6995dc96` does reference this PRD by id and label, but it was created from v1.2.0 after the reopen rather than refined against v1.1.0, and no beads issue or any other artifact in this repository referenced this PRD at an earlier version — so v1.2.0 remains the first version anything downstream was built from. The re-creation rule is therefore prospective — any TRD built from this document must be created from v1.2.0, and never refined against a superseded version. Approving roles for the individual decisions are in *Approvals and Decision Ownership*. A later requirements change reopens this document again and forces the same rule. As of 2026-11-14 one open question is carried forward — whether a future gateway-backed delivery adds its own requirement covering remote-gateway authentication — recorded in *Approvals and Decision Ownership* and in `TRD-2026-6995dc96`. Scope decision recorded 2026-11-14 (architecture owner, no version bump): the delivered kata integration is scoped to locally-spawned kata daemons; the remote kata gateway path is out of scope for this effort, undelivered and untested. The rationale, the two probe refusals behind it, and the open question it leaves for a future gateway-backed delivery are recorded in *Approvals and Decision Ownership* and in `TRD-2026-6995dc96`. This is a scope clarification plus a correction to the lock note above — no requirement or acceptance criterion changed — so `version` stays at 1.2.0 rather than signalling that TRDs must be re-created. Changelog v1.3.0 — 2026-11-14 Amendment recording the `tracker` contract bump that `TRD-2026-6995dc96` deferred to this PRD. Readiness 4.7 unchanged; requirements unchanged at 18; ACs unchanged at 58; ambiguity markers remain 0. `status` stays `Draft` — this document was already `Draft` after the v1.2.0 reopen, so recording a contract change here is not a lock transition. The rule this enacts. *Technical Constraints* states that a bump of either contract version "is a requirements change to this PRD, not an implementation detail," and *Open Question 12* records the labels decision as adding `tracker.label-one` to tracker contract 1.1 while deferring the bump itself: "Both bumps become a single PRD amendment owned by the architecture owner; this TRD does not bump either contract number on its own authority." This is that amendment, applied on the architecture owner's instruction. What landed. `packages/development/toolchain/categories/tracker.yaml` gains optional `tracker.label-one` (`inputs: [id, label]`, `outputs: [id, labels]`, `addedInMinor: 1`) and moves `1.0` → `1.1`. The *Technical Constraints* bullet and the *Dependency Map* row naming `docs/toolchain/contracts/tracker.md` now cite contract version `1.1`, keeping AC-001-4 and AC-015-1 pointed at a referent that matches the shipped contract rather than a superseded one. Why a minor bump, and why it breaks nothing. Adding an optional capability is additive, which `lib/toolchain/contracts.js#checkAdditiveOnly` permits within a major version; a major bump would be required only for a removal, a `required` flip, or a required addition. Compatibility is major-only, so the shipped beads adapter stays conformant at its unchanged `contract: tracker: "1.0"` pin, and `addedInMinor: 1` puts `tracker.label-one` in `checkCompat`'s `unavailableCapabilities` for it — beads cannot declare a capability it cannot honour. Scope of the bump. `tracker` only. The `work-graph` `2.0` → `2.1` bump the design also anticipates is not taken here: its motivation is additive *output* fields — `findings` on `work-graph.plan` and `dependencyAware` on `work-graph.graph-health`, per option C and the *Target Files* row "Work-graph contract amendment (AMENDED, additive)", to satisfy REQ-007 AC-007-3 and AC-007-4 — and those fields are produced by the shared analyzer work in TRD-016 and TRD-011, not by this change. `work-graph` therefore stays at `2.0` and this PRD's referent for it is unchanged. Downstream consequence, discharged rather than noted. The rule attached to *Lock history* says a requirements change here obliges `TRD-2026-6995dc96` to be re-created or explicitly re-confirmed. Re-confirmed rather than re-created, on the narrow ground that the only requirement touched is a referent version, not a behaviour: requirements, ACs, and the readiness gate are untouched, and the TRD's `tracker.label-one` design (TRD-012, TRD-033) anticipated exactly this contract shape. What must now change downstream is narrower and is recorded in the TRD, not here: statements asserting the shipped contract is still `1.0` and the amendment is pending are now false. Citation-safety convention respected. This entry cites constraints, dependency rows and Open Questions by quoted anchor. The PRD was previously edited using `PRD line NNN` citations in `TRD-2026-6995dc96`, which silently broke eight of them; this pass introduces none, and the two regions edited above the changelog are above the TRD's remaining PRD-line citation, so no anchor could drift. v1.2.0 — 2026-11-13 Refinement pass (`/ensemble:refine-prd`). Readiness 4.6 → 4.7. Requirements unchanged at 18; ACs unchanged at 58; ambiguity markers 0 → 0. Status reopened `Locked` → `Draft`. On the version: the skill's default for a refine pass is a patch bump, which v1.1.0 followed for two resolved markers and a new NFR cluster. v1.2.0 deviates deliberately and the deviation is justified by its own criterion — the bump is meant to signal "a requirements change, so TRDs must be re-created" — and this pass added a section, a delivery sequence, an external version floor, and rewrote three ACs. Nothing derived from v1.1.0, so nothing downstream is invalidated and the minor bump costs nothing. (`TRD-2026-6995dc96` does now reference this PRD by id and label, but it was authored from v1.2.0, so it is not a stale derivation; at the time of the v1.2.0 bump nothing in the repo referenced this PRD at all.) Reopened from Locked. The pass added a delivery sequence, an external version floor, and a constraints section, and rewrote three ACs. Under the lock's own definition that is a requirements change, so `status` moved to `Draft` rather than being quietly edited under a lock. Verified consequence *at the time of reopening*: nothing to invalidate — no TRD, beads issue, or other artifact in the repo referenced this PRD, so the re-creation rule bound only going forward. That condition no longer holds: `TRD-2026-6995dc96` was created from v1.2.0 and cites this document by id and label, so a future requirements change here obliges that TRD to be re-created or explicitly re-confirmed. New section — Technical Constraints and Dependencies. Previously absent: the PRD asserted a version gate (REQ-018 AC-018-2 "older than the version the adapter requires") with no version stated anywhere, and named its sibling PRDs only in frontmatter. Now sets the backing-tool floor at v0.23.0+ as the AC-018-2 referent — stated as a requirement this PRD imposes and the first implementation confirms, since nothing in the repo versions the tool — names the contract referents (`tracker.md` at contract version `1.0`, `work-graph.md` at `2.0`) so "the required set" is dated rather than moving, and carries a table of the five declared document/external dependencies with the requirement that enforces each. Implementation clusters → delivery waves. The five clusters were prose with no stated order. Now a numbered table: scope, requirements, start precondition, and the observable condition that closes each wave. Records that wave 3 (rename and prose) has no code dependency on wave 1 and can be built in parallel, that REQ-015 is deliberately last because it documents what waves 1-3 establish, and that REQ-016 is gated on an artifact existing rather than on a wave completing. REQ-017 bound given a shape: the requirement promised a "bounded" time and AC-017-1 required the error to name "the elapsed bound", but no bound or owner existed. Now states the bound is per capability class (read-only vs. tracker-writing/backlog-traversing), configurable per project, and always reported — with the seconds left to the TRD, since the right number depends on measured backing-tool latency. AC-017-1 asserts the capability, its bound class, and the bound in force. A Clarification note records that omitting the number is deliberate. Should-tier AC bar made explicit rather than implied: Notes now states 2+ ACs with an edge case for Must, 1+ for Should. REQ-008, REQ-014, REQ-015 and REQ-017 were checked against the Must-tier bar and left as they are, by decision. PRD Health Summary conformed to the create-prd metadata-only rule: dropped the restated Must/Should/Could/Won't and AC-coverage rows (REQ headings and AC sub-items are the source truth, and restated counts are what drift), added an open-clarifications row, and replaced the "see the Dependency Map section" pointer with the actual count — 27 cross-requirement edges across 14 mapped rows. Matches the sibling `PRD-2026-8d825f54` shape. Heading repaired: `## Approvals Decision Ownership` → `## Approvals and Decision Ownership`, restoring the conjunction every cross-reference in the document already uses. Readiness re-scored: Completeness 4.5 → 4.8, Testability 4.7 → 4.8, Clarity 4.5 → 4.7, Feasibility unchanged at 4.6; overall 4.6 → 4.7. Line-number citations from `TRD-2026-6995dc96` replaced with quoted anchors: the *Approvals and Decision Ownership* row, *Technical Constraints* bullet and Notes bullets added by the local-daemon scope decision inserted one line above the *Technical Constraints and Dependencies* bullet about contract-version bumps, shifting it and every later line down by one. `TRD-2026-6995dc96` cited this PRD by line number in eight places, so the cited passages moved — and two of the eight, at PRD lines 271 and 278 in Goals and Non-Goals, happened to sit *above* the insertion and stayed correct, which is exactly how this failure mode hides: the numbers keep looking plausible while pointing at the wrong sentence. No validator checks a prose `PRD line NNN` reference, so nothing fails. Each citation now names a quoted phrase from its passage, chosen to fit entirely within a single PRD line so that no future insertion can split the anchor itself. v1.1.0 — 2026-11-13 Refinement pass (`/ensemble:refine-prd`). Readiness 4.4 → 4.6. Requirements 15 → 18; ACs 48 → 58; ambiguity markers 2 → 0. REQ-004 marker resolved: in-progress status is represented by Kata item ownership — an owned-but-open item is the in-progress state; `closed` maps directly, `pending` and `done` map to open and closed. AC-004-2 rewritten to assert ownership rather than defer to an unresolved representation. REQ-007 marker resolved: graph-health is computed by the adapter as a local cycle and dangling-edge scan over the item links it already exports. Chosen over omission because no backing-tool command provides graph-health and the contract's links-only fallback implements only ready-listing and planning. Added AC-007-5 for dangling-edge detection. Goals graph-health bullet retained: it asserts that graph-health triage works on the new backend; the marker that made that an open question is now resolved, so the goal stands met by an adapter-side scan over exported item links rather than by a backing-tool command. New non-functional cluster E: REQ-016 (the skip guarantee extends repo-wide and the skips are proven honest, building on REQ-012 rather than repeating it), REQ-017 (bounded, observable adapter failures against a hung, failing, or unparseable backing tool), REQ-018 (unbound-workspace and too-old-tool misconfigurations caught in preflight before any write, scoped to what REQ-001/REQ-012 do not already cover). Three ACs each. AC-level implementation identifiers generalized: AC-001-1 and AC-013-2 named config-file and manifest identifiers (`toolchain.yaml`, `tracker: kata`, `work-graph`, `.kata.toml`), which belong at TRD level; both now describe the user-visible act. AC-013-4 keeps its literal `tracker`/`work-graph` keys, since reading shipped default configuration back is the observable check itself. Exit criteria 4-8 tightened to name what is observable, and criterion 9 added for the new robustness cluster; Dependency Map and implementation clusters extended to cover REQ-016/017/018.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-018-2: Given a backing tool older than the version the adapter requires | When preflight runs | Then it names the minimum version and makes no call that the old version cannot serve
- AC-001-2: Given the same project | When the toolchain preflight runs | Then the kata adapter's health check passes and reports the backing tool's version

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-001**: A Kata project needs no Ensemble-side behavior change to work its backlog. [Must] [RISK: adapter surface is large; a capability left unimplemented degrades silently into a fallback rather than erroring, so "coverage" must be asserted, not assumed]
A Kata project needs no Ensemble-side behavior change to work its backlog. [Must] [RISK: adapter surface is large; a capability left unimplemented degrades silently into a fallback rather than erroring, so "coverage" must be asserted, not assumed] The system ships a `kata` tracker adapter that declares both the `tracker` and `work-graph` categories and implements every required tracker capability plus every optional one whose contract names a fallback, so that selecting it is a configuration act and nothing else.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- AC-018-2: Given a backing tool older than the version the adapter requires | When preflight runs | Then it names the minimum version and makes no call that the old version cannot serve
- AC-001-2: Given the same project | When the toolchain preflight runs | Then the kata adapter's health check passes and reports the backing tool's version

--- TRD Context ---
**Verified baseline.** Read from the repository and the installed kata binary (v0.23.0 at `/opt/homebrew/bin/kata`).

- `tracker.yaml` v1.1 declares 18 capabilities: 4 required (`tracker.show`, `tracker.create`, `tracker.update`, `tracker.close`) and 14 optional, the newest being `tracker.label-one` (`addedInMinor: 1`) (`docs/toolchain/contracts/tracker.md:7`). `work-graph.yaml` v2.0 declares 3 optional capabilities, naming `work-graph-links-fallback` (`packages/development/toolchain/categories/work-graph.yaml:5-27`).
- Coverage differs by adapter. Beads declares all 17 tracker capabilities and all 3 work-graph capabilities (`packages/development/skills/adapter-tracker-beads/adapter.yaml`, `contract: {tracker: "1.0", work-graph: "2.0"}`). Jira (`packages/infrastructure/skills/adapter-tracker-jira/adapter.yaml`) and azure-boards (`packages/infrastructure/skills/adapter-tracker-azure-boards/adapter.yaml`) each declare `categories: [tracker]`, 8 tracker capabilities, and no work-graph capability.
- The graph fallback is partial. `work-graph-links-fallback` serves `ready` and `plan` only. `graph-health` returns `NOT_ALLOWED` (`packages/development/lib/toolchain/builtin/work-graph-links-fallback.js:279-287`), although the contract names this fallback for graph-health. `plan` appends unorderable items instead of reporting them (`:256`). The fallback orders topologically only when `tracker.show` supplies `dependencies` (`:311-322`). No shipped tracker maps that field, so the fallback is not dependency-aware on any shipped backend (reviewer-confirmed).
- Routing tests only the category claim: `trackerProvidesWorkGraph` checks `manifest.categories` (`packages/development/lib/toolchain/work-graph-resolve.js:77-79`). On that path `source` is the work-graph category default, not the tracker's (`:84`), which breaks AC-001-1.
- `tracker.list` with no `parse` block returns raw stdout (`packages/development/lib/toolchain/runner.js:1170-1171`). Beads, jira, and azure-boards leave it unmapped for that reason. A mapped list would be validated against `work-item.json`, which requires a top-level `id` (`runner.js:618-620`), so it fails unless `CAPABILITY_NORMALIZED_SCHEMA` routes it to a collection schema (`runner.js:601-604`).
  - Kata facts come from `kata <command> --help`, `kata quickstart`, and read-only `kata doctor --json` and `kata list --json` run in an unbound scratch directory, plus a live write-side capture in a scratch project bound with `kata init --project trd-capture-scratch` against kata v0.23.0 under an isolated `KATA_HOME` (2026-11-14; raw envelopes `~/.omp/trd-6995dc96/capture/*.json`, summary `~/.omp/trd-6995dc96/kata-envelope-facts.md`). Confirmed there: every envelope carries `kata_api_version`; the ref identifier is `short_id`; `--meta ensemble_external_key=<key>` round-trips as `issue.metadata.ensemble_external_key`; `list --meta k=v` filters exactly; `show.links[]` carries `{from, to, type}` edges; `list` returns `{complete, truncated, issues[]}` with no total; `close --evidence <type>:<value>` is accepted; `set-status` and a bulk or multi-id form do not exist. Kata still has no plan, graph-health, or export command and no type field. It has `ready` (open items not blocked by open items), blocking edges (`edit --blocked-by`), typed close evidence, and ownership (`claim`).

### Alternatives Considered

| Option | Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Manifest-only tracker adapter | `adapter-tracker-kata` declares `tracker` only. Work-graph stays on the built-in fallback. No engine change. | Smallest diff. Same shape as shipped jira and azure-boards. No new code path. REQ-013 trivially preserved. | Fails AC-001-1 and AC-006-2: the work-graph adapter resolved is the built-in, which reports its own identity and a default `source`. Fails AC-007-4: the envelope names the built-in, not kata. Fails AC-007-3 and AC-007-5: no graph-health source exists, because the built-in returns `NOT_ALLOWED`. Meets AC-007-2 only if kata's `tracker.show` maps `dependencies` [UNVERIFIED]. The PRD's own ACs still require the tracker amendments (AC-003-3 test evidence, AC-004-2 owner), so "no engine change" does not hold. |
| B. Graph operations on the tracker contract | Add additive tracker 1.1 capabilities `tracker.ready`, `tracker.plan`, `tracker.graph-health`. Leave work-graph untouched. | One category answers every tracker question. Independent of work-graph auto-routing. | Duplicates `work-graph.*`, so ready, plan, and graph-health each have two answers. Every graph consumer moves: `packages/development/skills/ensemble-beads-build-wave/SKILL.md:26` requires `work-graph.ready`, and PRD REQ-011 exists to prevent that churn. Kata still needs C's analyzer, so B pays C's engine cost plus a second surface. Contradicts REQ-001, which requires kata to declare the `work-graph` category. |
| C. Attach through `work-graph` v2.0 with one shared analyzer | Kata declares `tracker` and `work-graph`. `work-graph.ready` is native (`kata ready --json`). `work-graph.plan` and `work-graph.graph-health` declare `provider: work-graph-analyzer`, served by the existing built-in analyzer, extended with graph-health and findings. Contracts amended additively: tracker 1.0 to 1.1, work-graph 2.0 to 2.1. | Matches the PRD's declared categories. `tracker: kata` alone selects kata for both categories (AC-001-1, AC-006-2). Reuses the shipped ready and ordering code, adding no subsystem. Makes the graph-health fallback reference true. Beads (`bv`) and jira keep their current paths. | Three engine edits: resolver capability test and source fix, provider dispatch, and analyzer identity, graph-health, and findings. Plan and health cost one `tracker.show` per item unless `kata list --json` carries edges [UNVERIFIED]. The analyzer is shared, not kata-native, so the PRD must say so (Open Question 9). It changes jira's graph-health answer (Open Question 13). |

**Pick: C.**

**Rationale:**

- **Against A.** A is cheap because it stops short of the requirement. If A declares `work-graph`, plan and health have no provider and graph-health has no source. If A leaves work-graph undeclared, the resolved work-graph adapter is the built-in, so AC-001-1, AC-006-2, and AC-007-4 fail. The gap is computation and identity, not configuration. No YAML can emit a cycle finding, a `dependencyAware: true` for a backend with no plan command, or kata as the serving adapter. A also pays the tracker amendments (owner, close evidence), so the only work it avoids is the analyzer work that C needs too.
- **Against B.** B moves the same computation to another category and creates a parallel answer. Every consumer that requires `work-graph.ready` changes, and the analyzer is still required, so B costs C's engine work plus a second surface. It also contradicts the PRD's declared category set.
- **Why C adds the least machinery.** Each change extends a seam the code already has: a capability entry in `packages/development/toolchain/schemas/adapter-manifest-schema.json`, the in-process work-graph branch in `packages/development/lib/toolchain-cli.js:470-482` and `:539-547`, the analyzer that already computes ready and plan (`builtin/work-graph-links-fallback.js:211-258`), and the category contracts. No new subsystem duplicates `packages/development/lib/toolchain/`. Adapter directories hold data: `validateAdapterDir` (`packages/development/lib/toolchain/validate.js:762-788`) checks the manifest, allowlist, conformance, and credentials, and the runner executes only manifest argv templates (`runner.js:1261`). The one in-process capability path is the built-in module that `work-graph-resolve.js` already loads. A JavaScript module inside the adapter directory was therefore rejected.
- **The strengthened fallback.** Every work-graph answer states `dependencyAware`, and the serving adapter is named in the envelope. `plan` reports unorderable items as `findings` instead of appending them. Routing requires all three work-graph capabilities. No shipped tracker changes routing: beads declares all three, and jira and azure-boards do not claim the category.
- **Costs accepted.** C is the only option that meets the work-graph ACs, and the only one that changes engine code. Plan and health fan out one `tracker.show` per item. Each per-item call must share the capability's class bound, or N individually bounded calls are unbounded in total. The first implementation step measures this before the kata tests are accepted.
Satisfies: REQ-018, REQ-001
Target File: packages/development/lib/toolchain/preflight.js, packages/development/lib/toolchain/adapters.js, packages/development/toolchain/schemas/adapter-manifest-schema.json, packages/development/skills/adapter-tracker-kata/adapter.yaml
Actions:

Implementation AC:
- [ ] Given the kata manifest declares a minimum version of 0.23.0, when preflight reads kata --version reporting an older version, then preflight fails naming the minimum version and issues no further kata call.
- [ ] Given kata --version reports 0.23.0 or later, when preflight passes, then its record carries the reported version.
- [ ] Given a declared contract major for tracker or work-graph that does not match the category definition, when the adapter resolves, then resolution refuses on the major mismatch.

--- PRD Context ---
**Requirement REQ-018**: Selecting the new backend in a workspace it cannot serve must be caught before any work item is written. [Must]
Selecting the new backend in a workspace it cannot serve must be caught before any work item is written. [Must] Misconfiguration that REQ-001 and REQ-012 do not already cover — a workspace that is not bound, a tool version too old for a required operation — is caught during preflight, before the flow creates, edits, or closes anything. Goals and Non-Goals Goals A project selects its tasks backend by editing one configuration value, and the TRD-to-work-items flow works end to end on that backend with no beads tool installed. *(REQ-001, REQ-009, REQ-014)* Dependency-aware pickup, sequential planning, and graph-health triage work on the new backend, not only on the backend that shipped with the machinery. *(REQ-007)* No command, skill or agent name states which tasks backend it uses. *(REQ-009, REQ-011)* A project that never hears about the new backend sees zero behavior change. *(REQ-013)* The capability coverage of both backends is stated where a reader would look for it, and provably complete against the contract. *(REQ-015)* Non-Goals Making the new backend the default, or migrating anyone onto it. Selection stays explicit; unconfigured projects keep today's tracker. *(REQ-013)* A migration tool from Beads to Kata. Importing an existing `.beads/issues.jsonl` into a kata project, and the reverse, are out of scope; teams start a fresh backlog or keep beads. Third or fourth backends. Exactly two backends ship. The `jira` adapter stays as authored: it deliberately implements the tracker contract only and lets `work-graph` take the built-in analyzer. Nothing here pulls it onto the graph path. Changing what a TRD contains, or how it is authored. `create-trd` already reaches no tracker: it writes the TRD document. Requirement coverage, task format, shippable-state and design-readiness rules are unchanged. A compatibility window or deprecation period for the retired command name. Per the retirement precedent, removal is outright. *(REQ-009)* Scheduling, dispatch, retries, or recovery in Kata. Owning the work-item record is the whole claim; running agents against it stays outside Ensemble. Backfilling historical PRD and TRD documents. Archived documents keep their original wording, including the retired command name where they used it. Relationship to Existing PRDs Ratified in this run: this PRD extends the toolchain line of work rather than superseding it. The three documents below carry amendment notes at their next edit; none is reopened. | Document | Standing | Relationship | |---|---|---| | `PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer` | Locked, 2026-10-21 | Parent. Its exit criterion is that the tracker swap "is demonstrated end-to-end, by configuration alone", and REQ-020 already overrides the sole-execution-layer claim below. Kata is the second demonstration; it is the first that exercises the `work-graph` capabilities natively, which `jira` left on the built-in fallback. | | `PRD-2026-b6939c7c-config-driven-tools` | Draft, 2026-08-13 | Partially superseded, before this PRD. REQ-015 ("Beads remains the sole execution layer") and the non-goal "Migrating Beads off execution layer" were already overridden by 8d825f54 REQ-020. This PRD inherits that override and adds nothing new against it. Its Layer 1 and Layer 3 work — project-local configuration, provider-neutral prose, CI enforcement — is the foundation this PRD builds on, and its CI enforcement (no hardcoded backend references in prompts and skills) is treated as a check to satisfy, not a rule to re-litigate. | | `PRD-2026-023-multi-trd-beads-workstream` | 2026-06-16 | Non-goal conflict, resolved by scoping. Its non-goal "replacing Beads with another task graph system" is not contradicted: beads is not replaced, and stays default. Its multi-TRD workstream behavior is stated in beads terms; whatever of it must survive on kata is carried here as REQ-007 and REQ-008 rather than reopened there. | | `PRD-2026-87e64cc6-command-surface-consolidation` | 2026-10-06 | Precedent, followed. Its 2026-10-18 amendment retired variant commands by folding them into base-command flags and deleting the aliases outright, with no compatibility window (REQ-008 there). REQ-009 here applies the same retirement to the last backend-named TRD command. | Terminology. The user-facing request says "tasks backend"; the repository's toolchain axis is named `tracker` (category `tracker`, contract `tracker.md`, `tracker.*` capabilities), with `work-graph` as the dependency-graph category. This PRD keeps `tracker` as the technical name and treats "tasks backend" as the product-level phrase for a resolved tracker adapter. Approvals and Decision Ownership | Decision | Approving role | Criteria judged against | |---|---|---| | Adding a second tasks backend, and the adapter shape it takes | Architecture owner | `PRD-2026-8d825f54`'s locked contract; the constitution's approval requirement for architecture changes. Recorded as ratified in this run: extend, do not supersede. | | Removing a shipped command name outright | Command-surface owner | `PRD-2026-87e64cc6` REQ-008's no-compatibility-window precedent, ratified in this run. | | Keeping beads as the shipped default | Product owner | REQ-013; zero delta for unconfigured projects. | | Scope of native capability coverage in the new adapter | Architecture owner | REQ-001 AC-001-4 and REQ-015 AC-015-2: the required set plus every capability the contract marks with a fallback. Ratified in this run as tracker-plus-graph, not tracker-only. | | Whether the kata tool becomes a package dependency | Package owner | REQ-012; installation must not require it. | | Scoping the kata integration to locally-spawned kata daemons, leaving the remote kata gateway path undelivered and untested | Architecture owner | Decided 2026-11-14, recorded in `TRD-2026-6995dc96`. Two live gateway probe responses have no local analogue: sending no token gives `origin_forbidden`, sending a token that is not a valid browser session gives `web_session_required` — both `kind: internal` with `exit_code: 1`, both outside the 2/3/4/5/7 exit-code taxonomy this integration's error mapping assumes. The gateway also checks an `Origin` header the CLI controls, so an adapter cannot compensate by setting headers itself, which makes `KATA_AUTH_TOKEN` a hard prerequisite for remote use rather than an optional enhancement. Nothing below obliges anyone to reach or authenticate against a gateway. If gateway-backed delivery is wanted later, a requirement must be added covering remote-gateway authentication and its failure envelope: the 18 requirements here stop at "a Kata project" while the adapter manifest's `env` block already names `KATA_SERVER` and `KATA_AUTH_TOKEN`. | The accountable counterpart for the customer-facing approve/request-changes step is the same architecture owner who signs the adapter shape: no requirement here is approved by its author. Technical Constraints and Dependencies Constraints The backing tool must be at version v0.23.0 or later. This PRD sets that floor; it is a requirement, not an observation about the tool — nothing in this repository versions it, so the statement belongs here rather than in a lockfile. A bump of either contract version is a requirements change to this PRD, not an implementation detail. Beads remains the shipped default; nothing here licenses selecting the new backend by inference. *(REQ-013)* Delivery is against locally-spawned kata daemons. This effort configures, exercises and tests the adapter against a kata daemon started on the same machine as the flow that calls it; operation against a remote kata gateway is not delivered and not tested here. *(REQ-001, REQ-012, REQ-018)* Declared dependencies on other documents | Document | Role here | Enforced by | |---|---|---| | `PRD-2026-8d825f54-tool-abstraction-layer` (Locked) | Parent contract; its capability definitions and exit criterion are what this PRD satisfies | REQ-001 AC-001-4, REQ-015 AC-015-2 | | `docs/toolchain/contracts/tracker.md` (contract version `1.1`, amended 2026-11-14), `work-graph.md` (contract version `2.0`) | The required-plus-fallback-bearing capability set | REQ-001 AC-001-4, REQ-015 AC-015-1 | | `PRD-2026-b6939c7c-config-driven-tools` | Foundation: project-local configuration, provider-neutral prose, CI enforcement of no hardcoded backend references | REQ-011 | | `PRD-2026-87e64cc6-command-surface-consolidation` | Retirement precedent — outright removal, no compatibility window | REQ-009 | | `PRD-2026-023-multi-trd-beads-workstream` | Behavior carried forward in beads terms, re-expressed here rather than reopened there | REQ-007, REQ-008 | | Backing tool at v0.23.0+ (external, unversioned by this repo) | The operations the adapter maps onto | REQ-001, REQ-012, REQ-018 | Entry Criteria Before implementation starts: 1. The `kata` tool is available on the implementation machine, and a scratch kata project exists that a test harness can create and discard without touching a real project. *(prerequisite for REQ-001 through REQ-008; REQ-012 makes its absence a skip, not a blocker to the rest)* 2. The capability inventory in `docs/toolchain/contracts/tracker.md` and `work-graph.md` is confirmed current, since REQ-001 AC-001-4 and REQ-015 AC-015-2 assert against it. 3. The list of commands, agents and skills naming the beads-specific command is enumerated, so REQ-009's "no entry remains" is checkable rather than impressionistic. 4. Generation and validation entry points (`generate`, `validate`, the contract-docs check) are confirmed runnable locally, since REQ-009 and REQ-015 are asserted through generated artifacts. 5. A beads project fixture exists that exercises the TRD flow end to end, so REQ-010 AC-010-2 and REQ-011 AC-011-3 can be compared against before-and-after output rather than asserted from reading. Exit Criteria Effort is delivered when all of the following are observable: 1. Setting one configuration value in a project with no beads tool installed produces a scaffolded kata backlog with dependency edges, a ready list, and a sequential plan, from the backend-neutral command. *(REQ-001, REQ-007, REQ-009, REQ-014)* 2. A capability-coverage assertion passes for the kata adapter against the full required-plus-fallback-bearing set in both contracts, and fails when a capability is removed from the manifest. *(REQ-001 AC-001-4, REQ-015 AC-015-2)* 3. No source manifest or generated artifact names the retired command; the dispatcher rejects the retired name and names the replacement. *(REQ-009)* 4. The backend-neutral command accepts every phase the retired command supported, and a beads project produces byte-identical work items before and after. *(REQ-010)* 5. A project with no toolchain configuration resolves to beads, the shipped default configuration file is unchanged, and no tracker detection route selects the new backend from repository contents — a repository carrying a Kata workspace binding file with no toolchain configuration still resolves to beads. *(REQ-013)* 6. Installing the package and running its test suite on a machine without the kata tool both succeed, with kata-dependent checks reported as named skips. *(REQ-012, REQ-016)* 7. Shared command, skill and contract prose contains no tracker binary or tracker storage path outside explicitly beads-scoped sections, and the beads-scoped flow is unchanged by the prose edit. *(REQ-011)* 8. Generated contract documentation lists both backends with the native-versus-fallback split, and the docs check fails on an unrecorded manifest change. *(REQ-015)* 9. A misconfigured kata workspace stops in preflight having created zero work items, and a backing tool that hangs, fails, or emits unparseable output produces a named adapter error rather than a silent empty result. *(REQ-017, REQ-018)* Dependency Map | Requirement | Depends on | Reason | |---|---|---| | REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005 | REQ-001 | Each is a slice of one manifest; none is reachable until the adapter resolves | | REQ-006 | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005 | Fallback suppression is only observable once the capabilities the fallbacks stand in for exist | | REQ-007 | REQ-001, REQ-005 | Graph output is meaningless unless links land on real blocking edges | | REQ-008 | REQ-001 | Read paths ride the same manifest | | REQ-009 | REQ-001 | Retiring the backend-named name only makes sense once a second backend resolves | | REQ-010 | REQ-009 | Rename-and-preserve-flags is one edit; the flag set is measured from the pre-rename command | | REQ-011 | REQ-009, REQ-010 | Prose rewrite targets the neutral surface | | REQ-012 | REQ-001 | Absence handling is a property of the adapter's health and detection | | REQ-013 | REQ-001, REQ-012 | Detection-never-auto-selects matters only because a detectable candidate now exists | | REQ-014 | REQ-009, REQ-010 | Documentation describes the surviving command | | REQ-015 | REQ-001, REQ-006, REQ-007 | Coverage documentation records native versus fallback, which earlier requirements establish | | REQ-016 | REQ-001, REQ-012 | Skip-on-absence is only meaningful once there is a kata-dependent check to skip | | REQ-017 | REQ-001 | Timeouts and error passthrough are adapter behaviors, reachable only through its invocation layer | | REQ-018 | REQ-001, REQ-014, REQ-017 | Preflight gating reuses the adapter's health detection and the documented binding prerequisite | Delivery waves Shipped in this order. Wave 1 is the critical path; nothing downstream is observable until it closes. | Wave | Scope | Requirements | Cannot start until | Wave closes when | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Adapter manifest and mapping — one package, one manifest, one mapping table | REQ-001 → REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005 → REQ-006 | Entry criteria 1-2 met | Exit criterion 2 passes: coverage assertion green, and red when a capability is removed | | 2 | Graph capabilities — same package, separate capability group | REQ-007, REQ-008 | Wave 1: links land on real blocking edges | Ready list, sequential plan and graph-health all report the kata adapter as their source | | 3 | Surface rename and prose neutralization | REQ-009 → REQ-010 → REQ-011 → REQ-014 | Wave 1 in code no dependency; ships after it because REQ-009's premise is that a second backend resolves | Exit criteria 3, 4 and 7 hold; beads project output byte-identical | | 4 | Safety and disclosure | REQ-012, REQ-013 after wave 1; REQ-015 last | Waves 1-3 for REQ-015, which records what they established | Exit criteria 5 and 8 hold | | 5 | Robustness | REQ-017, REQ-018 after wave 1; REQ-016 once a kata-dependent test exists | Wave 1 for REQ-017/018; first kata-dependent test for REQ-016 | Exit criterion 9 holds | Wave 3 is the only wave with no code dependency on wave 1, so it can be built in parallel and held for ship order.
